summary: The starter prompt clearly defines the goal (a Python LlamaIndex RAG agent that stores chunked patient records with patientId and returns grounded, referenced clinical summaries) and the single-agent workflow. Many important engineering details (Python version, driver, exact embedding/chat models, index parameters, API surface, seed data shape and scripts, tests, and README/infra conventions) are not specified and will be chosen by the builder; these are predictable defaults but should be confirmed.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python LlamaIndex RAG agent that stores chunked patient records in a DocumentDB vector index... On request, retrieve the most relevant sections for a given clinical question... return a grounded answer with document references."

rubric.note: Single-agent RAG via LlamaIndex is explicit.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a modern Python 3.x runtime for developer machines; assume Python 3.10 (or 3.11) as the target for virtualenv and package installs.
rubric.note: Prompt says Python; skill.md confirms python/pip in a venv but gives no version.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use pymongo (MongoDB-compatible driver) pinned to a recent 4.x release (e.g. pymongo>=4.0,<5.0). For LlamaIndex store integration, use the latest compatible llama-index package (pin exact version in requirements.txt).
rubric.note: Neither prompt nor skill.md names the Python DB driver or versions.
skill.md explicitly describes a vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, DiskANN/HNSW/IVF support) and says use it.
skill.md instructs reading the cluster connection string from DOCUMENTDB_URI and to use a .env.example placeholder.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Model records with a patientId field for access control."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a collection named patient_records (or records). Each chunk document will include: _id, patientId, source_doc_id, chunk_id, text (chunk content), embedding (array of floats), metadata (dict), created_at ISO timestamp. No explicit shard key; single logical collection in sample_healthcare_01.
rubric.note: Database name is supplied by skill.md. The rest of the document shape and collection naming are not specified.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide a small synthetic dataset (e.g., 3–5 patients, 10–20 chunks each) included in repo under data/ with a seed script that is idempotent. Mark data as synthetic and MIT-licensed (or state "synthetic demo data") in the README.
rubric.note: No sample data source, size, license, or loading script specified.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "stores chunked patient records in a DocumentDB vector index"
rubric.skill_that_covers: skill.md (Run environment) -- cluster supports DiskANN, HNSW, IVF
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a cosmosSearch vector index of kind vector-hnsw (or vector-ivf) on the embedding field. Use similarity metric COS (cosine). Set dimensions to match embedding model output (assume 1536). Keep index parameters conservative for small demo dataset (default or small M/efConstruction values) and document in README how to tune for larger datasets.
rubric.note: Prompt implies a vector index but does not fix type, metric, dimensions, or parameters; skill.md only states what the cluster supports.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use OpenAI for embeddings and chat calls: embeddings model text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) and a GPT-style chat model (e.g. gpt-4o-mini or gpt-4o) for summarization. Expect credentials via OPENAI_API_KEY in environment. Integrate embedding calls where LlamaIndex expects them.
rubric.note: Embedding and chat model provider and exact models/dimensions are not specified.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "On request, retrieve the most relevant sections... and return..."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Expose a small HTTP API (FastAPI) with a POST /search endpoint that accepts JSON {patientId, question, top_k?} and returns JSON {answer, sources:[{doc_id,chunk_id,score,excerpt}], debug: {retrieved_count}}. Include a simple CLI wrapper for local demo runs.
rubric.note: Prompt implies an interactive request/response surface but doesn't choose API vs CLI vs UI.
skill.md instructs to use the existing reachable cluster and not to provision another one unless allowed.

rubric.skill_that_covers: skill.md (Run environment) -- suggests verification against live cluster
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide README commands: set env vars (DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY), pip install -r requirements.txt, python seed.py, uvicorn app.main:app --reload, and pytest to run unit tests (unit tests written to run without a live cluster).
rubric.note: skill.md includes verification guidance but not concrete commands to run the sample and tests.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Define Done as: seed script executed and populated sample DB (idempotent); /search returns a grounded clinical summary with document references and similarity scores for a given patientId; code runs locally with documented environment variables; requirements.txt pinned; unit tests pass locally without a live cluster.
rubric.note: Prompt describes desired behavior but does not give acceptance criteria or checks.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "clinical" context and patientId for access control
rubric.skill_that_covers: skill.md (Run environment) -- do not write connection string into files, use existing cluster
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Treat this as a demo/sample only (not production), do not provision cloud infra, keep dataset small to limit cost, avoid logging secrets, and note privacy/compliance non-goals in README (do not use real PHI).
rubric.note: Some run constraints are in skill.md; other non-goals (cost limits, compliance) are not specified.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Follow common sample layout: README.md, requirements.txt (pinned), .env.example, src/ or app/, data/, tests/, seed.py, and a top-level LICENSE (MIT). Mention use of the name "Azure DocumentDB" in the README and avoid alternate product names.
rubric.note: Prompt and skill.md hint at some conventions (.env.example), but not full repo layout or pinning policies.

contradictions: Prompt: "Using the DocumentDB skill" but the installed_skills list is empty. (There is a provided skill.md Run environment that documents the cluster and environment variables; confirm whether the prompt refers to that.)
questions_for_author: Which embedding and chat model(s) and provider should the sample use (exact model names)? This determines index dimensions and the env vars to document.
What application surface do you want: HTTP API (FastAPI/Flask), CLI, or a minimal web UI? This changes the sample structure and the routes/commands to implement.
Should unit tests be written to run entirely without a live cluster (mocking/patched client), or is a live-cluster integration test allowed for CI/local verification?
requirements_at_risk: A cosmosSearch vector index is created in code with dimensions matching the embedding model the app uses — prompt and skill.md do not specify index creation parameters or dimensions; builder will have to choose index kind and dimensions (at risk).

Retrieval runs the similarity search in Azure DocumentDB with $search / cosmosSearch — the prompt says use a DocumentDB vector index but does not require the $search/cosmosSearch API explicitly (at risk).

Retrieval is limited to the requested patient's records by patientId filter inside cosmosSearch — prompt requires patientId field but does not specify how to enforce filtering in the DB-level query (at risk).
The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository — skill.md covers DOCUMENTDB_URI but model credential env vars are not specified (at risk).
.env.example lists every setting with placeholder values — skill.md asks for .env.example but does not list every setting required (at risk).
Vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them — neither index parameter choices nor README guidance are specified (at risk).
One database client is created and reused across requests — neither prompt nor skill.md specifies client reuse patterns (at risk).
A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data — no seed script provided or specified (at risk).
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails — error-handling requirements are not specified (at risk).
Search results include the similarity score — prompt asks for references but does not require returning scores (at risk).
Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt — not specified (at risk).
Unit tests run without a live cluster — testing strategy is not specified (at risk).

Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type — skill.md says a cluster is already provisioned and does not ask to provide infra-as-code; the sample will likely not include infra code (at risk).
The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — not specified (at risk).
